mechanism: CDSE splits one agent skill into four parts: Meta (when and why to use it), Experience (lessons), Tool and Script. After each run it reads successful and failed trajectories, extracts text 'semantic gradients', and routes each to the matching part for a separate update and validation. An adaptive layer chooses which parts to load at invocation. Scores come from six agent benchmarks across three models.
claim: Beats the strongest competing skill-evolution method by 2.6 points on average across 36 settings and the base agent by 7.6.

idea_why: The split is plausible and cheap to copy in a skill folder, but the gain is only the paper's own claim.
breakdown: In a skill folder, keep separate files for when-to-use, lessons learned, tool notes and scripts. After each probe, a child reads the trajectory and proposes one edit to whichever file it belongs in, and a check reruns a past task before accepting the edit. The existing probe-to-verdict skill and its run logs already supply the trajectories.

mechanism: tmux holds named sessions in a background server, and 'tmux send-keys' types into a pane while 'capture-pane' reads its text. An agent can therefore drive or hand over a long-running terminal session, including one already logged in over ssh. The 'ceiling' in the title is that screen scraping gives no structured signal for when an agent is done or waiting.
claim: Guide to using tmux sessions and send-keys to run and hand over Claude Code sessions, with its limits.
why_not_testable: Body is thin and the guide was not read; tmux presence is unconfirmed and the hook blocks unattended terminal driving.
one_line: Comment thread points to a trick: log in yourself in a named tmux session, then tell the agent to take it over.
idea_why: send-keys and capture-pane are long-standing tmux features; the handover pattern keeps credentials out of the agent.
breakdown: Start a named tmux session, authenticate manually, then give the agent the session name so it uses send-keys to type and capture-pane to read the result. Poll for a prompt string to detect completion. Add a log file via pipe-pane for a durable record.
